summary: YANG-CBOR uses globally unique 63-bit YANG SIDs to identify YANG items, with allocation methods defined in RFC 9595. This Standards Track document uses those mechanisms to allocate ranges of 100 000 SIDs to Private Enterprise Number holders.

eli5.summary: Every company with a special number gets a block of ID numbers to name its own items.

questions: yang sid ranges for private enterprise numbers
how do you allocate yang sids
subtitle: Allocating globally unique identifiers to enterprise organizations through existing PEN assignments.

tldr.problem: Organizations need a way to allocate YANG Schema Item Identifiers (SIDs) for their own YANG models, but requesting new SID ranges requires coordination with IANA.
tldr.mechanism: This specification ties SID ranges to existing IANA Private Enterprise Numbers (PENs): organizations holding a PEN automatically get exclusive allocation of large SID ranges.
tldr.outcome: PEN holders can manage their own SID allocations without additional registration, reducing overhead and coordinating two registries.

today: RFC 9997 is a Proposed Standard and is the current specification for allocating YANG SIDs to PEN holders. It establishes the mechanism for automatic SID range delegation and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
YANG Schema Item Identifiers (YANG SIDs) are globally unique 63-bit numbers that identify items within YANG data models. RFC 9254 defines how to encode YANG data using CBOR (Concise Binary Object Representation) with SIDs, making the encoding much more compact than XML or JSON. RFC 9595 defines how to allocate SIDs using IANA registries.

This specification connects SID allocation to the existing Private Enterprise Number (PEN) registry, which has been maintained by IANA for decades. PENs are assigned to organizations that need a private namespace for their own specifications, much like organization identifiers in other systems.

The scheme allocates SID ranges to PEN holders: each organization holding a PEN below 1,000,000 gets exclusive use of 100,000 consecutive SIDs, with a representation size of 64 bits. Organizations holding a PEN below 100,000 also get a smaller range of 10,000 SIDs with a 32-bit representation size, which is more efficient for encoded data.
sections.eli5: YANG uses short numbers to name different parts of data models. Instead of creating a whole new system to give out these numbers, the plan reuses the existing company ID system (PENs) so each company automatically gets its own block of numbers to use.

sections.title: Key Concepts
sections.content:
The specification uses two mega-ranges allocated by IANA:

  • 32-bit SID range: 3,000,000,000 to 3,999,999,999 (1 billion SIDs). These SIDs require only 32 bits to represent in CBOR, making them highly compact. Allocated to PEN holders with PEN values below 100,000.
  • 64-bit SID range: 300,000,000,000 to 399,999,999,999 (100 billion SIDs). These require 64 bits to represent. Allocated to any PEN holder with a PEN value below 1,000,000.

Within each mega-range, SIDs are allocated using a formula based on the PEN value. For a PEN holder with PEN value ppp ppp (less than 1,000,000), the 64-bit allocation gives them SID numbers 3pp ppp p00 000 through 3pp ppp p99 999 (100,000 consecutive numbers). For PENs less than 100,000, the 32-bit allocation additionally grants 3 ppp pp0 000 through 3 ppp pp9 999 (10,000 numbers).
sections.eli5: Organizations get two pools of ID numbers: a large pool (using 64 bits) and a smaller, more efficient pool (32 bits) if they have an older company number.

sections.title: Allocation Example
sections.content:
RFC 5612 reserved PEN 32473 for use in examples and documentation. Under this specification, a holder of PEN 32473 would be allocated two ranges:

  • The 64-bit range from SID 303,247,300,000 to 303,247,399,999 (100,000 consecutive SIDs)
  • The 32-bit range from SID 3,324,730,000 to 3,324,739,999 (10,000 consecutive SIDs)

Since PEN 32473 is designated for documentation and examples, these SID ranges are also marked by IANA as available for use in documentation and examples.
sections.eli5: A company with a low ID number gets to use special ranges of numbers in both the large and compact ID systems.

sections.title: Design Rationale
sections.content:
This allocation scheme offers benefits and tradeoffs:

  • Low-friction assignment: PEN holders automatically receive their SID ranges with zero additional overhead. The PEN registry uses a low-threshold process requiring minimal paperwork.
  • Representation size tradeoffs: The 64-bit SID range is large enough for most use cases, but the encoded representation takes 8 bytes. The smaller 32-bit range (for PENs under 100,000) encodes in 4 bytes, reducing CBOR message size. This benefits constrained devices but is expected to be exhausted around 2040 as new PENs are allocated.
  • Discovery challenges: A PEN appearing in a SID does not guarantee the SID originates from that PEN holder—it is merely a namespace convention. PEN holders should provide their own public repository or YANG library to help others discover their models.
  • No land grab expected: Although the PEN registry has existed for decades with no surge in speculative registrations, the specification acknowledges that assigning number spaces might theoretically encourage requests. However, historical evidence suggests this is not a practical concern.
sections.eli5: This approach is simple and automatic, but the company still needs to publish a list of what each number means, or users won't find the definitions.

sections.title: IANA Allocations and Management
sections.content:
IANA allocates two mega-ranges in the YANG-SID Mega-Ranges registry and applies specific management policies:

  • The 1-billion-SID range (32-bit) starting at 3,000,000,000
  • The 100-billion-SID range (64-bit) starting at 300,000,000,000

Within each mega-range, each PEN holder's individual SID block is delegated to the PEN holder themselves under a "Private" allocation policy. This means the PEN holder controls how SIDs within their block are assigned to their own YANG modules or sub-organizations. Management authority is derived from IANA's demonstrated capacity to maintain the PEN registry for several decades, ensuring sustained technical support for at least 10 years (the required duration for IANA mega-range operators).

IANA also marks two example ranges (based on PEN 32473) as Reserved for Documentation, making them available for use in RFCs, examples, and documentation as stated in RFC 5612.
sections.eli5: IANA set up the system and made sure each company could manage its own block, relying on IANA's long track record of maintaining the company ID system.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 9595 and RFC 9254 apply to this allocation mechanism. The key concern is that appearing in a SID does not prove provenance: a PEN value embedded in a SID does not guarantee that the YANG module actually comes from the PEN holder. Potential attackers could use SIDs in the allocated ranges without authorization.

To mitigate this risk, PEN holders are encouraged to provide publicly discoverable information about their YANG modules, either through a public repository (such as GitHub) or by publishing a YANG library (as defined in RFC 8525, or a constrained version in a separate specification). Implementers that use PEN-based SIDs should also provide YANG library information to help consumers verify that they are using authentic modules.
sections.eli5: Just because a number belongs to a company doesn't mean something is really from that company. Companies should publish a list of what they actually made so people can check.
